title: Verify and land Claude agent-state hooks for Remote Sessions
body:
Land the parked work that gives a Claude Remote Session its agent-state badge (working / needs you / idle), now that it can be verified. The code already exists as ONE commit, 0d34db3 on branch card/sfyaz0 ("Launch-time Claude hooks and the Tunnel's /hook route"): --settings hook JSON added to a bare Claude launch on a Posix Remote, each hook one curl to the Tunnel, and a POST /hook route feeding the existing hook lane. It was never merged because its acceptance needs Stop and PostToolUse observed from a real logged-in Claude on a Remote, and Claude there was not logged in. It is logged in now. main has moved 15 commits since (git merge-tree reports no conflict), including a bounded-drain rewrite of src/control/tunnel.rs, a remote::relaunch / agent_of predicate, install Sessions with no Tunnel, and a structural "no network under test" guard (remote_probe::spawn_network / network_allowed).
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (sections: Agent state, The way back, Results). Read docs/agent-state.md first, then the foreman-agent-state-campaign skill. The original card's criteria: `foreman kanban list sfyaz0 --json`.
Blocked by: Visual second pass: Remotes page and folder picker in foreman's row grammar
Do:
1. Bring 0d34db3 onto your branch (cherry-pick it; do not rewrite it into something else first). Re-read it against today's main and fix what moved: the /hook route must use route() / build_call() and every refusal must go through the existing bounded-drain path with the short pre-auth head deadline; a caller with no token gets the same treatment as the other routes; an install Session (remote::install_of) and a non-agent launch get NO hook settings; a reconnect (remote::relaunch) of a Claude Session gets the hook settings again with the NEW token; a wrapped agent that relaunches bare gets them too. Nothing under cfg(test) may spawn a process or open a socket outside the guard. Full suite green before going further.
2. Verify against the real Remote. The test Remote is andy@192.168.8.168 (hostname Falador, Debian, key login, never ask for a password; `claude auth status` there now reports loggedIn true; Claude Code 2.1.105). You are running inside the INSTALLED foreman, which does not have this feature, and the human has a dev instance open that you must not touch. So build and run your OWN instance:
   - build: cargo build --release --target-dir target/agent/hooks (never target/, never target/agent/build which the human's dev instance holds)
   - give it its own config so it cannot clobber anyone's workspace: create target/agent/appdata-hooks/foreman/, copy ONLY settings.json from target/agent/appdata/foreman/ into it (that file has the Remote named falador), and launch the exe with APPDATA set to target/agent/appdata-hooks
   - launch it with a clean environment the way scripts/run-dev.ps1 now does (read its launch section: it strips FOREMAN*, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_PID, NO_COLOR, GIT_EDITOR, GIT_ASKPASS, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, KITTY_WINDOW_ID, TERM, COLORTERM). Record its PID.
   - drive it through ITS control pipe, not yours: its pipe is named foreman-ctl-<pid>-* (list \\.\pipe\ in PowerShell); set FOREMAN_PIPE to that name, unset FOREMAN_PROJECT_ID and FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID, and use the exe you built as the CLI. It will open with no Projects; open one on a scratch directory first if `open` needs one (see `foreman --help` from your exe).
   - on the Remote use a throwaway directory /tmp/foreman-hook-test (create it over ssh; remove it at the end). Open a Claude Remote Session there with a small prompt that makes Claude use one tool (for example: list the files here, then say done). The folder-trust prompt will appear the first time: that is the needs-you case, so observe the badge BEFORE answering, then answer it in your own probe Session with `send`.
   - evidence to capture, with timestamps, from `status --json` on that Session (agent_state field) and from `snapshot`: working after the prompt is submitted (UserPromptSubmit), still working across the tool call (PostToolUse), idle when the turn ends (Stop), needs_you on a permission or trust prompt if the events support it, and no agent_state for a plain Remote shell. Also run a prompt that makes Claude spawn a subagent if you can, and record what the subagent's hook payloads look like, to answer the spec's subagent filtering question.
   - confirm from the Remote side that nothing was installed there: no foreman files, no change to ~/.claude/settings.json (compare its mtime or content before and after).
   - then close your Sessions, stop YOUR instance by its PID only (never by name), and remove /tmp/foreman-hook-test on the Remote.
3. If an event does not arrive or maps wrongly, fix it and re-verify. If something cannot be verified, say exactly what and why in the final report and in docs/agent-state.md; do not claim it.
4. Docs and skills: commit 0d34db3 already adds Remote gotchas to docs/agent-state.md; correct them to what you observed. docs/remote-sessions.md says "Agent-state badges are not available on a Remote Session yet", and both providers' dispatch and chat skill copies say there is no agent_state on a Remote Session: update all of them to what is now true (Claude on a Posix Remote: yes; Codex and Grok: no hooks in this card; Windows Remotes: untested / not built), following the embedded-skill rebuild rule in the foreman-docs-and-writing skill. Add a Results entry to the spec with what was run and seen.
5. Commit body: state what was observed for Stop, PostToolUse and the subagent payloads.
Do not: launch Codex with its hook-trust bypass flag; install anything on the Remote; touch the human's dev instance (target/agent/build, target/agent/appdata) or stop any foreman by name; ask for a password.
Done when:
- the hook settings are on a Claude launch and reconnect and on nothing else (unit tests), the /hook route refusals are bounded (socket tests), and the full suite passes
- Stop and PostToolUse were observed from the real Remote and the evidence is in the commit body and the spec's Results
- docs/agent-state.md, docs/remote-sessions.md and the four skill copies say what is true; cite-guard is clean
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
